entries.name: Lady Senara of Hindon (heiress/ward)
entries.status: ALLY — chose to sacrifice her childbearing to end her blood-curse (rite at midsummer); rift with Elidyr over it
entries.dossier: Idnerth's only child (~19; mother long dead, no brother). Now Abisec's ward; hostile [Fate No, solar 482] — charged him with overturning God's judgment, certainty cracked when told the truth (incl. Achil's abduction, confirmed by Custennin) but not her hatred; rejects his wardship. On the road her father did NOT free her of the lie [Fate No]; Custennin will carry the truth after the burial. MATERNAL kin: royal-descended, the old line at EBBESBORNE, but headed by the wastrel LORD CADELL ('judged unfit'), who WON'T press for her [Fate will-press No, 34] — her hoped refuge is a hollow door; royal blood only makes her a richer marriage-prize (no land descends past the attainder [Fate No]). PARDONED by the King (482) — blood clean, attainder lifted; remains his sworn charge. Ulfius openly named the move: a marriage (Abisec×Senara) would unite deed-claim + blood-claim and end the quarrel — she still hates the man who broke her house. The marriage angle is live; she's hostile. She is a weapon either way — the Crown's marriage-pawn to 'clean' a Hindon grant, or a Morgan-shaped grievance pointed at the men who broke her house, Abisec foremost. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): Abisec offered her genuine CHOICE (back any path — convent, marriage, uncle's hall, Hindon, revenge on Gwythyr, even a marriage-knife) instead of disposing of her — cracked her guard [Honest 18 vs Suspicious 14, won partial]. Took her to Idnerth for the truth; Idnerth ExcNo'd [98] — recanted Gwythyr, named Abisec the wolf, counselled wed-and-ruin-from-within (the Morgan path is now her father's deathbed advice). She believes him → re-hardened. Abisec kept the oath with honor and withdrew [Honor success, rolled 1] — a hairline counter-crack. Marriage/agency offer open; she's hostile but conflicted. — Uther (482): her person/keeping stays Abisec's charge, but her HAND is the Crown's — the King warned Abisec off the marriage. She may ride to London for her father's end under guard. (Abisec's 'no one — the King's' to her holds true.) — Summer 482: watched Idnerth executed (unrepentant); then declined BOTH flight and her father's undermine-Abisec counsel [returns ExcYes; scheme No]. Came back composed, clean-handed, the old certainty spider-webbing. A genuine (if quiet) turn away from the Morgan path — open which way she breaks. — First court (482): she tested Abisec publicly; he passed (true justice, not her father's protect-the-useful-liar). Her first concession ('He'd have kept him... you are not what he told me'). The arc turns — hostility breaking toward something unnamed; not won, but no longer his enemy in her own mind. — Marriage-politics (Roderick, summer 482): Uther TORN on Abisec×Senara (aggrandizement vs. locking her loose blood-claim to a loyal man). Gettable as the King's gift on terms; a rival suitor (Gwythyr) reaching for her would tip Uther to allow it to Abisec instead. With Senara thawing, the match is quietly becoming viable on both the Crown and personal sides. — HINDON HOMECOMING, the keep wall (autumn 482): Abisec answered her honestly (justice done, but the master still at large), then took the homecoming bread & salt up to the rampart, gave her room, and asked how it had truly been for her. She did NOT fully open up [Fate Likely→No 54] — too proud, the wound too fresh — but gave the shape of it level & controlled ('the maids don't know what to call me — half think me a prisoner'; 'a fine thing to learn at nineteen the hall you were proud of was built on stolen silver'). The thaw HOLDS and warms a notch on one thing: Abisec's offer to recall her confessor **Father Custennin** landed ('the one face here that was never pretending') + 'thank you for asking; no one else has thought to.' Trust earned in inches, not poured out. She won't be rushed. — UPDATE (483 spring): given true agency by Abisec (apology + choice), Senara chose to seek a MARRIAGE OF HER OWN rather than stay a ward at Hindon — she wants her own household/standing and out from under the house that broke hers. NEW TASK for Abisec: advocate a decent match for her to Uther (her hand is the Crown's). The Abisec×Senara match: declined by her in all but name. — KING'S WORD (483 spring, Sarum): Abisec advocated a decent match for her (pointedly NOT himself) [Fate No 62]. Uther REFUSED to spend her on a comfortable match AND declined to push the Abisec match [Fate No 67] — instead he APPROVED that Abisec didn't grab her blood-claim (it keeps Abisec a dependent Crown tenant, not an independently-legitimate lord) and on that logic RESERVED her hand as a Crown asset: 'royal blood is spent where it buys the Crown the most; she marries when I've a use for her, to the man that use names.' So Senara's fate stays the King's — the disposal-without-say she dreads. Abisec kept his word to ask but cannot deliver her hope. EMBER: the Crown will marry Senara off for politics on Uther's timing. — ESCALATED (summer 483): Custennin (her confessor) confirmed the wound is structural (she needs real agency, not kindness) and warned — from outside the seal — that she is PAST GRIEF and has already BEGUN to act; the window to reach her is closing. NEW sub-mystery: what is Senara DOING (her own hand, built sideways from inside)? The crux for Abisec: find something REAL to give a Crown-controlled ward, fast. — CRUX CLARIFIED (summer 483 confrontation): Abisec's realest offer (blunt friendship + back ANY path she names) nearly reached her [Fate No 34] but she skewered its flaw — his help ends at the King's word, and the one path she'd walk (a husband & house of her own) the Crown already denied. THE OBSTACLE IS THE KING'S RESERVATION OF HER HAND. To truly reach/save her, Abisec must take that on with the Crown (dangerous; Uther reserved her deliberately). She's 'making her own way' now and won't show it (Morgan hand building). Until the King's wall moves, she's unreachable & a sharpening danger. — THE MAN NAMED (GM, summer 483): she loves SIR ELIDYR of the Ebble (minor but greatly-respected house, near her mother's Ebbesborne kin); the King forbids it (her blood too dear for a minor house); she plans a SECRET ruinous marriage. Abisec deduced a man exists [Fate No 80 — she won't name him, won't trust his promise to defy the King]. RESCUE PATH: find/confirm Elidyr + actually WIN the King for an open match (proving resolve by ACTING, since she won't trust a promise) before her secret wed-and-ruin plan detonates. — THE STAKES & THE CLOCK (summer 483, Custennin+Eluned): if Senara weds Elidyr in secret against the Crown's reserved right, it is a THEFT OF A ROYAL RIGHT — and Abisec, her keeper, wears it: shattered royal favour, a ruinous fine, HINDON endangered (held on a conditional vow, forfeit twice as fast if turned), and the deadly suspicion he CONNIVED (Uther Trusting 6). A consummated clandestine marriage is canonically UNBREAKABLE — fixable only BEFORE, never after. Her self-ruin = Abisec's ruin (+ Achil's inheritance). CLOCK: NOT imminent [Fate No 23] — months of runway. THE ONLY CLEAN PATH: make it LEGAL — win the King's LEAVE for the Elidyr match — which means finding UTHER'S PRICE for giving up a blood-card he's hoarding. Forcing/chaining her only proves her right & spurs her. Eluned's lead: find the man in the EBBLE country (her mother's world), NOT through Senara (she'd feel it & bolt). — IMPASSE (summer 483 confrontation): Abisec's fullest relational appeal (vulnerable honesty + Custennin witness) FAILED [Fate No 82] — she denied the betrayal-frame (his kindness = the bars; she stood in his hand, not beside him). Words are exhausted. THE FORK IS NOW FORCED: (1) FIGHT THE KING for her (find Elidyr + Uther's price; the hard/right road), (2) TURN HER OVER to Uther as his direct ward (shed the liability; cold/safe; quietly or with a warning), or (3) step back (months exist, but inaction still risks Abisec's ruin). She faltered once at Custennin's appeal — not beyond all reach, but not by talk. — CONFIRMED (summer 483 ultimatum): offered name-the-man OR swear-before-God-not-to-defy-Uther, Senara [Fate No 40] refused the oath (devout — won't perjure) and thereby CONFIRMED to Abisec's face, before Custennin, that she WILL defy the King; still won't name the man. She nearly broke (wept) but chose her plan ('not sorry enough to stop'). Abisec gave every fair chance — the decision is now his & morally clean: FIGHT THE KING for her (find Elidyr + Uther's price), TURN HER OVER (now with airtight justification — she confirmed the threat before a priest; warn or quiet), or step back (clock runs). — EBBLE INQUIRY FAILED (summer 483): Abisec + Custennin rode the valley to find the man [Fate No 77] — the Ebble gentry CLOSED RANKS, not against the question but against ABISEC'S NAME (the King's hand that broke her house & holds her; they won't sell a beloved local lord & pitied girl to him, fearing he'd break the match too). The door's there but barred to his reputation. REDIRECT: Custennin alone, priest-to-priest with the local clergy, can likely unlock the village talk (general knowledge, no seal broken) — days + Abisec's absence the price. The slog deepens (records dead-end, then the knight's inquiry); the man (Elidyr) stays just out of reach — making the 'turn her over' road look ever simpler. — THE MAN FOUND (summer 483): Abisec's deadline-gambit (telling the Ebble she goes to Uther in days, the match's hour now-or-never) FLUSHED ELIDYR OUT [Fate Yes 22] — Sir Elidyr of Throope came forward, worthy & genuine, now Abisec's ally. Abisec now HAS the man Senara wouldn't name. The path to the legitimate match is open — pending the King's leave (find Uther's price). Senara still confined, unaware Abisec found him. — THE MATCH GOES CLEAN (summer 483): Elidyr is RODERICK's vassal (Abisec's mentor-liege) & would quitclaim any Hindon blood-claim — so the match is Roderick's to broker and the claim-risk to Abisec's caput is cageable. The path now runs through RODERICK. ONE WALL STANDS: the KING's price (Uther won't release her royal blood to a minor house without a reason; the Gwythyr-coin is too thin yet). — TURNED (summer 483) [ExcYes]: Abisec ACTED (found Elidyr) and it reached her where words never did — Morgan path arrested, trust restored, she'll wait; now his partner not his adversary. THE REMAINING WALL: the King's price (Roderick judges the play not-yet-ready). NEXT: strengthen the hand — develop Gwythyr SMOKE→PROOF (the decisive coin + nails a hidden traitor + checks the rival) OR find Uther a real PROFIT in the match — then win the King's leave. **SUMMER 483:** the turn held & deepened. Elidyr poisoned by a hidden hand; Senara kept the sickbed vigil, fought off the night-killer (with Custennin & the watch), and gave Abisec the key read: 'Elidyr hadn't an enemy in the world — whoever did this struck at ME, through him.' Abisec rode to Hantonne & back and SAVED Elidyr. She owes him her hope's life; the alliance is now proven in blood. Wall still standing: the King's price for the match. **(scene 40) HER CALL:** offered, then held to, the keeper's rite — barrenness by her own choice, for the valley & her freedom, not for Elidyr (rejecting his veto). A reclaiming of the blood that owned her. Rift with Elidyr left raw.

entries.name: Marriage / the dynasty (Adwen at Wilton; Senara)
entries.status: active — heir URGENT; no higher match (land-light); Roderick counsels a solid match now (nods to Eilwen)
entries.dossier: Heir urgency sharply up — Abisec nearly died at 23 with no heir; the line currently falls to brother Achil. Live prospects: SENARA of Hindon (would end the Hindon quarrel & unite the claims, but hostile); LADY NEST of Tisbury (genuine spark, door ajar — she wrote asking how he mends; her test is whether his danger is temporary); LADY GENERYS (Caradoc's daughter — old-guard alliance, may warm as Caradoc thaws; faith-tension); LADY ADWEN (Wilton widow, a £12 dower manor in hand, but a feud with her dead husbands' kin — 'come back when you've done your sums'). No heir yet. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): the Abisec×Senara route is now CROWN-BLOCKED — Uther reserved Senara's hand to himself and warned Abisec to his face off marrying her (don't unite the deed-claim with the blood-claim). So Senara is off the marriage table unless the King wills it. Live prospects narrow back to Nest (door ajar), Generys (warming as Caradoc thaws), Adwen (Wilton widow). Heir still urgent. — UPDATE (summer 482): Abisec's RISE reframes the whole market — a banneret-castellan is now a catch; Eluned: 'go choosing, not begging.' The field: NEST (door now OPEN + genuine liking — Eluned's pick); GENERYS (Caradoc's price met → could heal the old-guard feud; devout/faith-cool); ADWEN (called on, Courtesy 18 → receptive; a real partner + £12 manor, but the Goronwy-kin FEUD attached); new — LADY EILWEN of the western march (safe, clean dowry, alliance on the Gwythyr flank; green, unmet). Abisec's to choose. — RODERICK'S COUNSEL (Sarum, summer 482): as a TENANT-IN-CHIEF, Abisec's marriage is now semi-political — a knight's daughter Uther ignores, but a powerful match (a great honour / baron's heiress) needs the King's leave and will spook him (he denied the barony to keep Abisec dependent; same logic as blocking Senara). 'Marry small and stay free; marry big and wear the King's leash.' Roderick's lens: GENERYS mends the old guard (he'd welcome it); NEST safe & decent (Crown indifferent); ADWEN — don't buy a 2nd feud; EILWEN — useful flank but ropes him west into Summerland/Gwythyr's weather + Cadwal's troubles. Roderick will smooth a knight's-daughter match, OR make quiet inquiries for a higher Crown-friendly house IF Abisec wants to aim up (bringing Uther into it). Open question to weigh: what should the marriage DO — heir, peace, land, or power? — Roderick will QUIETLY LOOK AROUND for a higher Crown-friendly house (a season+ to bear fruit; a background process). And the SENARA option is reopened on new terms (Roderick's read): Uther isn't flatly against Abisec×Senara — he's TORN between (a) not wanting Abisec aggrandized (deed+blood = over-mighty) and (b) wanting the loose Ebbesborne blood-claim LOCKED to his loyal gate-holder rather than seized by a rival (Gwythyr). So the match is gettable — but only as the King's GIFT on the King's terms (humble petition, framed as Crown-security not self-gain, outliers stay Crown's, a tighter leash). THE LEVER that would tip Uther to YES: a rival (Gwythyr) reaching for Senara's hand. Combined with Senara's own thaw, the once-poison match is turning real from both ends — the most powerful but most Crown-entangled card in Abisec's hand. — (scene 8 denouement, 482): Abisec lightly asked the King about Senara's future; **Uther unmoved** [Fate Unlikely→No 70]: he keeps her hand RESERVED to the Crown (her Ebbesborne royal blood 'worth keeping, not spent in haste'), neither granting the Abisec match nor closing it — 'she's safe as your ward; leave it there.' The match stays Crown-blocked but not dead; Abisec's risen stock did NOT soften him (granting the heiress-ward mid-inquiry would look like self-dealing). Status quo: Senara a thawing ally & a deferred possibility, not a present prospect. — UPDATE (483 spring): SENARA has removed herself from Abisec's own marriage options — given the choice she asked to be married OUT (her own house, away from wardship), not to Abisec. Abisec's heir-question thus narrows back to the other prospects (Nest open; Generys cool; Adwen+feud; Eilwen free) or a Crown/Roderick-brokered higher match. Abisec now also owes the Crown an advocacy on Senara's behalf. — UPDATE (483, King's word): Uther RESERVED Senara's hand as a Crown asset (won't grant a decent match, won't push Abisec) — her marriage is now a Crown-politics ember on Uther's clock, NOT in Abisec's gift. Notably Uther signaled he PREFERS deed (Abisec) and blood (Senara) kept SEPARATE — keeps Abisec a dependent tenant. Abisec's own heir-search stays among the other prospects / a brokered match. — RODERICK'S WORD (483 spring, Salisbury) [Fate No 56]: NO higher match landed. He fished — floated a clever, ambitious court-favourite lady — but she asked after Abisec's LAND, found it thin, and is promised higher. The honest reason: Abisec is GLORY-RICH but LAND-LIGHT, holding Hindon on Uther's vow (not his own deed), so great houses circle but wait to see if he lasts before binding to him (and Uther prefers him un-over-mighty). **Roderick's counsel (mentor):** the HEIR is urgent (Abisec near-died sonless at 23; line hangs on unbelted Achil) — take a clean SOLID match NOW and get sons; leave the grand marriage for the heir or for a richer future. He NODS to EILWEN of the march (clean, a western tie, no feud) over any court-cat. The decision is Abisec's. Live solid prospects: Eilwen (free, clean, march alliance — Roderick's pick); Nest (real liking, less political); Generys (cool, old-guard mend); Adwen (willing, feud attached). — UPDATE (483 spring): Abisec chose to HOLD & consolidate (no marriage yet; deepen land/standing, let the high houses come to him) — but a friendly call on Cadwal FIRMED the western-march alliance AND upended his lukewarm read of EILWEN [Fate ExcYes 5]: at ease she's striking, frank, and hard-won honest (fled the forced marriage, survived rough, freed herself) — a kindred spirit and now the most compelling prospect he has (heart + march + substance). The 'hold' still stands by choice, but Eilwen is now a real pull, not a dutiful fallback. — UPDATE (May-eve 483): Abisec tried to redirect EILWEN to his heir Achil (ages 16/17) — NO spark [Fate No], and Eilwen read the sidestep as a dodge, cooling her regard for Abisec. So Eilwen is neither Achil's match nor (now) cleanly Abisec's; the heir-question is unresolved and Abisec's best real connection is stung. SENARA is firmly OFF (and now adversarial-leaning). — UPDATE (May-eve 483): EILWEN resolved to a clean, warm NON-MATCH turned FRIENDSHIP/ALLY [Fate ExcYes] — Abisec dealt straight (age + different wants); she values her hard-won freedom over any marriage now. So no prospect landed this spring: Senara OFF (adversarial-leaning), Eilwen a friend not a wife. The HEIR remains UNSOLVED and urgent (Roderick's counsel stands) — prospects Nest (real liking, untested lately), Generys (cool/old-guard), Adwen (willing/feud), or a brokered match remain for a future season. Abisec kept his integrity and gained a march ally instead of a bride. — (note, summer 483) Abisec's OWN heir still unsolved, now entangled: the Senara/Elidyr crisis must be resolved (legitimize the match, win the King's price) before it ruins him; only then back to his own match. **SUMMER 483 — a great new shadow:** MERLIN has revealed he wants Senara's royal Ebbesborne blood for an unnamed design and OPPOSES the Senara–Elidyr match [Awareness✓]. The kingmaker is now quietly against the very union Roderick blessed — a power far above the King's mere 'price.' **RIDDLE OF MERLIN'S OPPOSITION — CRACKED (scene 35-36):** not politics — COSMOLOGY. Senara's blood carries an Otherworld changeling-pact (see #24); a child of it could 'open the door' for the wild against settled Logres. Merlin (builder of the human realm) won't have that issue bred to an uncontrollable love-match. The match is thus entangled with the pact: to free Senara to wed Elidyr may mean SHUTTING THE DOOR FOR GOOD first. **(scene 40) The King's-price problem may DISSOLVE itself:** if Senara does the rite & is known barren, she's worthless to Uther as a royal match → he'd free her hand. But the rite may cost her ELIDYR (he won't wed a woman who gutted herself 'for him'). The external obstacle traded for an internal one.

entries.name: Idris's death (the barrow; Gwenllian's unpaid debt)
entries.status: active
entries.dossier: Sir Idris ap Cynan died in the storm of Hindon (482) taking a spear hauling Achil out; Abisec's First Aid failed (roll 18). Buried in a barrow on Salisbury Plain, his name in the county roll. On the road home Abisec offered to help bury him and pay respects, but Idris's mother GWENLLIAN (Cynan's widow, who lost her only son) rebuffed him cold [Fate No, 77] — 'lords always have friends to dig for them, and brothers who come back.' The debt to Idris's memory / to Gwenllian sits UNPAID.

entries.name: The second doubted lord (Idnerth's unproven charge: Gwythyr)
entries.status: active — the KEY to the King's price (if proven): develop the gentry-smoke into real proof of Gwythyr's treason → worth a boon (Senara's match)
entries.dossier: Uther set his snare for TWO lords. Idnerth wore the Boar; the OTHER was never named at the time. Spring 482: the dying Idnerth NAMED him — GWYTHYR OF MERE — claiming they 'sounded each other' a year back and Gwythyr let him take the bait, now inheriting the valley with the King's eye fixed on the dead Boar. UNPROVEN (no seal, no proof). Roderick does NOT credit it [Fate No] and forbids speaking it without evidence — 'a knife with no handle.' A weapon against the rival if ever proven; poison to Abisec if wielded unproven. Open. — UPDATE (Sarum 482): Abisec REVEALED the Gwythyr naming to Senara (bending Roderick's keep-it-sheathed order). Confronted, IDNERTH PUBLICLY RECANTED it before Senara & Custennin ('I named no one; said it to soften the wolf') — the charge now actively DENIED by its own source. Abisec did NOT press it ('I'll not gainsay a man at his pass'), re-sheathing the lead. Net: Abisec still privately credits it (Idnerth named Gwythyr unbought in the cellar), but it's now discredited to Senara and any third party — murkier and harder than ever to wield. Still unproven. — Idnerth now DEAD (executed unrepentant, London, summer 482) — the only mouth that ever named Gwythyr is silenced and recanted; the lead is as cold as it gets, live only as Abisec's private conviction. (Meanwhile Gwythyr's men probe Hindon's western bounds.) — Note: Gwythyr reaching for Senara's hand (to revive the valley-claim through her Ebbesborne blood) is now a live danger — AND paradoxically the lever that would make Uther grant her to Abisec instead. Watch the careful man's marriage-moves. — REOPENED (summer 483) [Random Event: Move Toward Thread + Inquire·Cooperation]: Sir Elidyr of Throope, trading good-faith coin to earn Abisec's help with Senara, surfaced that the old honourable Ebble/Ebbesborne houses long WATCHED Baron Gwythyr of Mere dealing with Idnerth in the years before the Boar's fall — 'ways the gentry whispered and none dared say.' Corroborates the dying Idnerth's 482 naming of Gwythyr as Uther's OTHER doubted lord. Elidyr offers to tell Abisec all he knows. A fresh, cooperative lead on the long-cold suspicion — AND potential LEVERAGE for the King's-leave bargain (Gwythyr is now Abisec's graduated rival + a possible hidden traitor). — CORROBORATED but UNPROVEN [Q2 No, summer 483]: Elidyr's full account = the gentry watched Gwythyr's riders on Hindon roads, an unexplained Mere↔Idnerth closeness, wool/coin moving the wrong colour through Idnerth's factor, before the Boar's fall. Aligns with the dying Idnerth's 482 naming → Gwythyr the LIKELY 2nd doubted lord. But it's a TRAIL, not a proof (no letter, no witness who'd stand before the King) — NOT yet the coin to buy the King's leave. To become leverage it needs developing into real proof (a future intrigue). — STRATEGIC PIVOT (summer 483): Roderick killed the idea of trading it UNPROVEN to Uther (backfire). But if DEVELOPED into real proof, exposing Gwythyr as the 2nd doubted lord is a service worth any boon — incl. the King's leave for Senara's match. The Gwythyr-proof arc is now tied to the Senara rescue (the likeliest coin for the King's price). **FACTION TURN (summer 483) — Gwythyr moves to 'Destroy the Foe':** sensing Abisec circling, the careful baron works off-screen to DRY UP the gentry-smoke against him — leaning on the old Ebble houses to silence the very whispers (Mere↔Idnerth) that are Abisec's only trail. The proof Abisec needs for the King's price just got harder to gather; the clock favours Gwythyr.

entries.name: Old-guard friction (Caradoc, thawing)
entries.status: RESOLVED (held) — Caradoc & the old guard WON outright (summer 483 strand victory): 'the old guard's yours, lad'
entries.dossier: The old guard distrusts Abisec's fast royal-favoured rise. Caradoc's price was 'prove you'll last / hold a thing.' Then Abisec set his body against a baron in God's trial, took a lance through the chest, and lived — and now holds Hindon — and even Caradoc allows 'the boy has bottom.' Valour (and land) doing what charm couldn't. The Generys marriage-door may warm with the father. — FLARED (summer 483 war-council): Caradoc voiced the old-guard preference for the established Gwythyr over the banneret-of-a-spring-ago to command the western host — the thaw tested again, on a war footing. Winning Caradoc could flip the command question. — THAWED (summer 483 council): Abisec's critical plan won old Caradoc outright — 'there's the years and the land I feared you lacked, lad; they were in your head the whole while.' The old guard's price ('prove you'll last, hold a thing') paid in full. Friction largely resolved; Generys door warmer by association. — Further sealed (summer 483): Abisec ceding the WON van to the veteran Gwythyr killed the old guard's last doubt (that he'd climb on steadier men's backs) — Caradoc's warmth now real.

entries.name: Hold & build Hindon's caput; Gwythyr's grudge
entries.status: active
entries.dossier: RESOLVED in Abisec's favour (the hearing, 482): the King created Abisec Knight Banneret and granted him Hindon's CAPUT to hold for the Crown on his sworn perpetual-fealty vow; Gwythyr DENIED the valley; Senara pardoned. The full barony / Council seat NOT granted — the outliers stay in the King's hand, a thing to grow into by service. THE CAPUT: £55 (shell-keep castle DV 9/13/2 + a Mill + the wool market-town + home manors). THE OUTLIERS (NOT his): ~£95 in 8 parcels, escheat to the Crown, 'in question' only until Idnerth's vertict, then settled-forfeit — the King will likely break them up / feed a parcel to Gwythyr. STRATEGIC WEIGHT: the Hindon valley is the gate between Salisbury and Summerland (Cadwy's Mendip silver/lead Uther seized); Gwythyr holds Mere, the other gatepost. TO DO: harden the caput modestly from his own purse (~£50 plan — dammed town-moat, palisade + gatehouse round the wool-town, deep cistern, two towers); stout vs raiders/a rebel, useless vs a king's host (loyal initiative, not a power-base). Live successors: Gwythyr's grudge (the slighted, careful rival); the second-lord suspicion still unproven. Levers held: the storming + exposing the Boar; the King's favour; Roderick + Ulfius; the march. — UPDATE (spring 482, Abisec in seisin): the BOLT is UNDERWAY (£37) — wall + fortified gatehouse + wet moats around both town & keep + a drawbridge linking them (mill-stream dammed); core by raiding season, done by autumn. Household bound (Bledig sworn & retained under Mabli; Alun/Madog/Elad garrison; Sioned's infirmary — Hindon's healing name spreading). Toured town & villages [Courtesy 18: success] → wary folk WARMING (a lord who walls their homes beats a baron who taxed for his gilded hall). HOOK: a western hamlet's reeve confided that GWYTHYR'S men have been 'riding the bounds,' asking after an old boundary stone by the beck — the careful man testing the new neighbour's edges. ~£103 liquid left. — FIRST COURT held (summer 482): household oaths sworn publicly (Bledig seneschal, Mabli steward, garrison); mill-toll CUT for a year + hand-quern outlawed (relief + the lord's mill-right); the moved BOUNDARY STONE ordered restored to the true line & FENCED (a clear, lawful signal to Gwythyr's probe — the new neighbour counts his yards); a systematic wool-factor fraud exposed [ExcYes] & justly ruled (restitution+stocks+banishment, life spared at the commons' ask). Net: the valley's commons WON (a lord who asks, repays, and gives justice — loyalty no wall buys), the wool-staple's honest name restored. Gwythyr's grudge & border-probe still live.

entries.name: Stapleford pagan scandal (CLOSED)
entries.status: closed
entries.dossier: CLOSED (Plough Monday 481). Cynfael deflected; Iuan installed as a tolerant resident priest; the rite continues quietly. Watch: Cynfael will pounce on any future slip.

entries.name: The Boar Conspiracy (CLOSED)
entries.status: closed
entries.dossier: The central thread of 480–482, finished. ORIGIN (480): a royal courier on Salisbury Plain murdered and a sealed dispatch stolen by trained British-tongued men; Abisec ran them down, recovered a secret royal muster-order AND a snare — Uther binding trusted lords while secretly testing TWO doubted lords, one bearing a Boar badge; an informant inside Roderick's house had warned the Boar-lord early. CHAIN: Father Maucan (Vagon's chaplain, the informant, paid in boar-coin — captured, broken); Sir Cadeyrn (handler/grey-rider — captured, defiant); Baron Idnerth of Hindon, 'the Boar' (one of the two doubted lords). Trial-by-combat lost (Twelfth Night 481; Abisec maimed). But the Boar's abduction of Achil (482) handed Uther his pretext: a royal commission, the Salisbury host, and the STORM OF HINDON — Abisec planned and led it (deception + escalade), took Idnerth alive in single combat on the burning wall, and gave him to the King's justice rather than a knight's sword. Idnerth → Londinium cell & scaffold. COST: Sir Idris ap Cynan dead in the rescue. (Disposal → Hold-Hindon thread; the heir → Senara thread.) Loose ends: who else Master Gwyn's ledger named; the wider spy-network.

Abisec won the King's trust [opposed Honest 13 vs Suspicious 14 — won]; Uther counts him 'an honest instrument I can spend without watching my back,' honoured the Roderick chain, charged him as the Twelfth Night witness. Royal favour gained.

entries.name: The western march, bought — an innovative outside syndicate
entries.status: active — the master STRUCK FIRST (silenced the Bristol lead); the hunt is now MUTUAL
entries.dossier: NEW THREAD (Turning Point on the altered homecoming, summer 482 — Thread NEW; Plot Points: Home Sweet Home / Sold! / Organizations In Conflict invoking Lady Eilwen). A clever OUTSIDE money-power [Faction goal: Inside Enemy Territory; tag: Innovative] has bought a foothold on the WESTERN MARCH around Sir Cadwal: bought up his debts, a mill & two fee-farms, and CONTRACTED Lady Eilwen's hand (Sold!) to their man — fast, by coin and contract, not charter and sword. The march is in uproar (Organizations In Conflict): Cadwal's house split, neighbour knights enraged that land & a bride changed hands for money. GM TRUTH [Fate No, 42]: it is NOT Gwythyr — a genuinely new power; Mabli reads it as a mercantile/financial operation, no Logres baron's style. WHO is behind it = unknown, to investigate. STAKES: Abisec's western flank infiltrated, a marriage prospect (Eilwen) taken, Hindon's own wool-economy a plausible next target. (Gwythyr at Mere will hate this incursion too — odd-bedfellow potential; the Crown, fresh off the Summerland accord, would mislike a destabilised march.) — INTEL (Mabli/Senara/town merchants, summer 482) [Mabli Stewardship 15: success]: PROFILE — a mobile, ruthless, OUTSIDE-FUNDED merchant-company [faction tags: Innovative, Mobile]; the coin is foreign (foreign weight to the silver, via cross-water channels — not valley/Sarum/London money), purse origin OUT of Logres, into the dark (deep mystery). METHOD — picks indebted minor march houses (more name than coin), buys the debt → the debt forces the marriage → the marriage takes the land; LAWFUL every step (Senara's read), which is why the sword-lords can't fight it ('you can't lance a contract'). AGENT (the loose thread to pull) — a brutally competitive merchant-factor who keeps HIRED MUSCLE; brusque, foreign coin, mobile (3 manors poorer in his wake). The wool-town fears it's next & asks if Abisec will stand for them. LEADS: pull the agent; follow the foreign coin to its source. — PLAN (summer 482): Abisec rates the DIRECT threat to Hindon LOW (the syndicate preys on the weak/indebted; Hindon is solvent, fortified, with a 6-knight eschille) but the strategic threat real (flank eroded, isolation, reputation) — and a useful counterweight to Gwythyr. Chosen response: INVESTIGATE + build a MARCH COALITION (be the protector the alarmed leaderless knights/barons lack — a defensible power-base under 'the King's peace'). Senara's steer: Cadwal is broken/useless; the rally-point is old BARON MEURIG (lost no ground, furious, the lesser houses follow him, knows every house's debts) — approach him as one who'll STAND FOR the march, not swallow it. — CADWAL'S TRUTH (summer 482) [Abisec Courtesy 18: success]: the method confirmed — his small honest debts were bought up at once into one fist, squeezed, then the agent offered 'mercy' = forgive all for Eilwen's hand + the manor. THE LEVER: it's all CONTINGENT ON THE DEBT — redeem Cadwal's debt (~£60) BEFORE the wedding and the marriage-contract collapses (the agent holds paper, not a wife). Agent due back to collect by HARVEST. Paying it = shatter the syndicate's claim here, free Eilwen, bind a grateful house on the weak flank, and PROVE to the watching march the syndicate can be beaten (coalition fuel) — at the cost of most of Abisec's ~£99 liquid. The deeper purse/master behind the agent remains unknown. — THE NUMBER IS A FORGERY (summer 482): Abisec smells the £60 — a small honest debt (~£12-15 over three lean years) bought up, then bred to threescore in one spring by interest-on-interest + INVENTED 'costs/fees' Cadwal never agreed to. [Fate Yes, 13: provable FRAUD, not mere lawful usury.] NEW & BETTER LEVER: don't pay the £60 — PROVE the fraud (needs Mabli + the debt-papers) → the debt dies, the contract dies, Eilwen walks free, and the syndicate stands exposed as FORGERS (a hanging matter; coalition fuel; lawful weapon). Cheaper than £60, far more dangerous to them — they won't take exposure quietly. THE GROOM [npcs roll]: an ambitious young FOREIGN merchant on the make (clothes 'like nothing worn this side of the water') — coin & foreign coin marrying into the noble blood to seize the manor; a clue to the syndicate's outland origin. NEXT: secure the ledger/evidence; Mabli builds the fraud case; choose the venue to break it (manor court / Roderick / the Crown); the agent returns by harvest. — MABLI'S VERDICT [Stewardship 15: CRITICAL] + THE MARCH'S STATE [Fate ExcNo, 88]: (1) WEAPON — Mabli proves the £60 forgery cold AND finds it's the SAME forging hand/method across many march houses' consolidated debts: a TEMPLATE, not a one-off. So the proof that frees Eilwen can VOID EVERY contract bought on a forged debt — the whole land-grab unmakeable at law (a court/Crown matter; forgery is a hanging crime). She's pulled a thread toward the forger's own hand (a lead toward the syndicate's centre). (2) BUT TOO LATE TO SAVE FORWARD — the syndicate moved fast (Mobile); most vulnerable Selwood houses are ALREADY fallen this spring (Maiden Bradley, Stourton, Kilmington — gone, wed off or turned out). Cadwal is near the last still saveable. PLAN INVERTS: not rescue-the-next-victim (coalition of sufferers mostly gone) but REVERSAL + EXPOSURE — break Cadwal's contract as the first domino, then use the systematic-forgery proof to unwind the purchases wholesale, restore the dispossessed, and rally them + the un-bought (MEURIG) behind the man who unmade the forgers. Venue TBD (shire court / Roderick / the Crown). Agent due by harvest. — INSIDE MAN FOUND (summer 482): a courtesy call on BARON TEWDWR OF WERESIDE [Awareness 13: success] reveals him as the syndicate's COMPROMISED NOBLE COVER — a debt-drowned royal-blooded wastrel they cooped (not devoured) to lend legitimacy & look away while they harvest his peers (foreign plate/coin in his hall; evasive on 'the newcomers'). A WINDOW into the syndicate + a LEVER (his ruinous secret), to work once Abisec's no longer his guest (Hospitality/Honor binds him now). RISK: Tewdwr may tip the syndicate to Abisec's poking. — MEURIG WON (summer 482) [Abisec Courtesy 18: success; honest pitch — forgery + asked his counsel]: the coalition SPINE secured. He'll lend weight + bring WITNESSES (wronged/dispossessed houses to swear the forged debts on relics) — turning the legal case into a march-wide reckoning. He does NOT suspect Wereside [Fate No] (Abisec's inside-man card stays private). CRITICAL STEER — THE SHERIFF IS SUSPECT [Fate No, 48]: Meurig distrusts the King's new shire-sheriff (untested, soft, Uther's centralizing appointee) and suspects he's BOUGHT — reasoning that ink-and-forgery could only eat a whole march 'lawfully,' deeds in order, if the officer who registers them is paid to look away. Implication (unproven, chilling): the syndicate's reach may run into the King's own administration — which makes it squarely a CROWN matter. PLAN: do NOT take the proof to the sheriff (it'd vanish + warn them); go OVER him to RODERICK (honest Count, his shire, Abisec's patron) → the KING. Free Cadwal as the first domino; muster Meurig's witnesses; carry the wholesale-forgery case up the ladder. Agent due by harvest. — THE KING'S COURT (midsummer 482): Abisec lodged the case (Roderick presenting) and FUMBLED the presentation [Courtesy: fumble, 20] — Uther's paranoia flipped the loyal play into 'who's been mastering my march behind my back, the thieves or you?' Recovery TIED [Honest 18 vs Suspicious 14 — no resolution]: his honesty stopped the fall but didn't dispel the suspicion. Then Abisec's SAVE [Courtesy 18: success, rolled 1] — instead of Roderick's surety, he asked the King to make NO ruling, only to SUMMON Cadwal + the foreign groom and judge for himself (the groom being Uther's would-be vassal — the King's own interest to vet him), framed as loyal duty. Uther embraced it (a paranoid test-loving King handed control). OUTCOME: the matter is now a CROWN MATTER — to be TRIED before the throne, Cadwal + the foreign groom summoned; Abisec to bring Mabli's forgery proof + Meurig's witnesses; the King's own eye (Intrigue 23) the blade. The syndicate's agent must answer a Crown summons or brand himself by fleeing. The voided lands will be Uther's to keep or grant. NEXT: marshal proof + witnesses for the royal trial; the sheriff & foreign-purse may surface under royal scrutiny; free Eilwen via the verdict. COST: Abisec's royal favor recovered from the brink but is now WATCHFUL, not easy. — THE CELL TAKEN (scene 7, midsummer 482): forewarned within two days of Abisec's audience (Meurig's read: the leak is the King's hall or the bought sheriff's rolls), the factor LIQUIDATED & RAN — dumped the Stourton mill, Kilmington fees, and Cadwal's debt-paper cheap to a Bristol buyer for portable silver, and let Eilwen's bride-contract LAPSE (Eilwen effectively freed pending the verdict). Abisec ran him down at a ford [chase CRITICAL] and took him ALIVE with the LEDGERS INTACT + the strongbox + 4 prisoners. The factor admitted he is only a CUTOUT for a principal ACROSS THE WATER whose name Abisec does NOT have, and offered to inform for his neck; Abisec REFUSED and delivers him WHOLE to Uther. STATE NOW: the Crown trial is imminent with defendant + physical proof + Meurig's witnesses converging at Sarum; the deep mystery (the foreign master overseas) PERSISTS; the bought sheriff unresolved; Gwythyr's spite a fresh black mark. — THE CROWN TRIAL WON (scene 8, midsummer 482): order = cold proof [Mabli Stewardship 15 → 18 FAIL: dry paper alone nudged Uther's suspicion] → the wronged men [Abisec Courtesy 13 → 1, strong success: a dozen relic-sworn dispossessed turned it, and the ledgers became corroboration] → the factor brought out BLIND [Q1 No: he won't lie into an unseen net, folds & confirms; Q2 No: a TRUE CUTOUT — cannot name the master]. VERDICT: forged debts void root & branch; bought lands restored to the turned-out; Eilwen free in law; factor + swords condemned; the foreign groom damned by his flight. The LOCAL land-grab is UNMADE and justice done. BUT the master across the water stays FACELESS ('a house behind three houses') — the deep mystery persists only as a cold documentary trail in the seized ledgers (a future hook for Mabli + cross-water inquiry). Down-weighted to a simmer. — LEAD WARMED (scene 14, autumn 482): where the captured factor was a true cutout (nothing), the inside-man GETHIN's seized records gave a concrete CROSS-WATER lead — a name in Bristol, a wharf, the man who carried the foreign silver across the water. The cold ledger-trail to the master is WARM again: a thread to pull (Mabli + a Bristol inquiry). The master himself still faceless, but the next rung is named. — THE MASTER MOVES (483 spring) [faction turn: Destroy the Foe]: he silenced the Bristol wharf-man (drowned, Gwyn-signature) before Abisec could run the lead — the warm trail goes COLD, but the move proves the master is real, close to the western water, fast, and AWARE he's hunted. The hunt is mutual; Abisec may now be a foe to be destroyed in turn. Possible tie to the guided-raiders (#21 — his western channel?).

entries.name: The factor's flight — the syndicate's march-cell breaks
entries.status: resolved (cell broken — scene 7, midsummer 482)
entries.dossier: RESOLVED (scene 7, midsummer 482): both choke-point gambits FAILED [Meurig No 49 — men too scattered to watch the Severn in time; Gwythyr ExcNo 97 — refused the rider, let the factor cross Mere unhindered to spite Abisec]. Abisec ran him down alone [Horsemanship 15 −5 → check 10: CRITICAL] at a ford SHORT of the water, the silver-mules bogged at the crossing. The eschille routed 4 hired swords (2 down, 2 yielded); the factor surrendered hands-open. Cell BROKEN; ledgers seized INTACT before the river + a strongbox of foreign coin + 4 prisoners. Abisec REFUSED the factor's bargain and delivers him WHOLE to the King [Honor/Just]. Closed; the trial + the still-unknown foreign master carry forward on thread #14.

entries.name: The bought sheriff — rot in the King's new county system
entries.status: RESOLVED — Gethin caught & rendered; sheriff Pasgen cleared
entries.dossier: NEW THREAD (Crown trial, scene 8, midsummer 482): the trial exposed that the syndicate's forged deeds were registered 'lawfully' by Uther's new shire-sheriff (a 482 GPC appointee — 'sheriffs appointed across Logres'). Baron Meurig had named him bought; the King, hearing his own officer let a foreign power eat a march under the King's seal, said aloud 'someone in my own house was paid to look away' and will move on him. OPEN: is the sheriff a paid traitor or merely a fool the syndicate used? Either way it implicates the new county system (Uther's centralizing reform) and may be a thread back toward the faceless master. Abisec, who broke the case, is the natural man for the King to set on it — or to be tarred by, if the rot runs near. — COMMISSION ACCEPTED (scene 8 denouement): Abisec honestly flagged his own conflict — he holds Hindon now, so hunting the sheriff invites the charge that he & Meurig schemed for the seat [opposed Honest 13 vs Uther's Suspicious 14 → both succeed, King edges it; Abisec partial: honesty respected, not doubted, but the suspicious King keeps control]. Uther structured it CLEAN: Abisec FINDS the rot, Crown officer **Sir Brewnor** (no stake, owes Abisec nothing) WEIGHS it and renders to the King; neither Abisec nor Meurig touches the seat or the silver; 'if the rot runs toward you, Brewnor finds that too.' So: trust + a leash. THE INQUIRY: how deep does the bought sheriff's corruption run in the new 482 county system — a paid traitor or a used fool? — and does his cross-water paper trail run back toward the faceless master? Abisec charged; Brewnor partnered; not yet begun. — DEFERRED LAND-REWARD (denouement): Abisec asked about the recovered march-lands; Uther won't deed march-acres to the man investigating the march's officer ('settle the sheriff clean — then we'll see what's in my gift'). So the ownerless escheated parcels (Stourton/Kilmington/Maiden Bradley etc., now in the King's hand) are a POSSIBLE reward GATED behind clean, vindicated completion of the sheriff inquiry. Incentive aligned: do it clean, and land may follow. — AUTUMN DOWNTIME (scene 10): Abisec tended home a few weeks; thread-pressure check — the sheriff did NOT move [Fate Likely→No 78]. He sits tight: holds his courts, seals his rolls untouched, either unaware Abisec specifically has been set on him (the commission was kept quiet) or wagering the forged deeds look lawful enough to survive scrutiny. The rolls are intact, the trail still warm — the delay cost nothing. Brewnor relays it. — INQUIRY OPENED, first push FAILED (scene 12, late autumn 482): Abisec questioned Cadwal (circumstantial only — he never saw the sheriff; the factor + a shire CLERK stamped the forged deeds through 'in an afternoon, no questions, like he'd done it a hundred times — too fast') and rode the shire-town with Meurig + Brewnor. **TWIST [Fate 50/50→No 77]: the sheriff Pasgen is NOT complicit — a soft, frightened FOOL whose SEAL was used, not the mastermind.** The real rot is the 'second hand under the seal' — a clerk/deputy/under-sheriff conduit (unidentified). **FIRST PUSH FAILED [Abisec Intrigue 11→18]:** riding in openly with a march baron handed Pasgen a martyr's part — he cried persecution ('the Hindon faction comes to take the county the way he took Hindon'), the shire-clerks closed ranks, doors shut. Brewnor (dry) read Pasgen as a fool & warned Abisec the optics backfired — exactly the conflict Abisec flagged to the King. NEW SHAPE: clear the fool, find & prove the real conduit — quietly, via Brewnor's impartial authority + Mabli's forensics, NOT a baron's open ride. RISK: Pasgen's persecution-cry may reach Uther (reviving 'watch your hands'); the conduit is now forewarned. — RECOVERY (scene 13): Abisec PUBLICLY cleared Pasgen & apologized in the shire-court yard [Courtesy 13→6 success]: the optics flipped (no martyr to a knight who clears him), the closed doors opened, and Pasgen — flooded with relief — turned cooperative, FLINGING his office open to clear his name. He named the prime 'second hand': his under-clerk **GETHIN**, who kept the seal-keys unwatched while Pasgen rode circuit ('he knew I never read past the wax'). So the real conduit now has a likely IDENTITY (Gethin) + the office is open to Abisec/Brewnor/Mabli. The 'watch your hands' risk EASED (a public just act reads well to Uther). NEXT: prove Gethin is the bought conduit & take him (forewarned — may have covered tracks/fled); chase his Bristol/cross-water link toward the master. — CLOSED (scene 14, autumn's end 482): Abisec delegated cleanly (found the rot = his commission; let Pasgen+Brewnor+the King take & judge — no seat-grab) and rode home. OFF-SCREEN [Fate 50/50→ExcYes 1]: Pasgen & Brewnor took the under-clerk GETHIN at a river-stair a day from fleeing (saddlebag packed, Bristol passage paid); confessed, convicted, rendered to the King in irons. Pasgen fully CLEARED & grateful. Abisec's hands clean (the King's law, not his). BONUS (ExcYes): Gethin's records opened a WARM Bristol cross-water lead (a name, a wharf, the man who shipped the foreign silver) → feeds thread #14. Royal favour eased off probation; the King's deferred land-reward now in view. Thread resolved (w0).

entries.name: The western-march affinity (Abisec's power-base)
entries.status: active — Abisec's emerging march power-base
entries.dossier: BORN at the Hindon dinner (late autumn 482): Abisec feasted the march's grateful & un-bought — Meurig, Cadwal (+ freed Eilwen), and ~6 restored knights whose fields the trial gave back — and bound them to him [Courtesy 13→4 success]. Meurig pledged it aloud: 'the march had no spine this spring; it has one now — Hindon's.' A real network/affinity now looks to Abisec as the march's protector under the King's peace — allies to call on (men, witnesses, news, standing). The thing he set out to build. Watch: a marcher affinity is also the kind of 'over-mighty' shape a paranoid Uther & a slighted Gwythyr both notice. — LESSON (483 raid): Abisec raised Meurig's muster but got NO word back during the action — when Gwythyr (the great baron) and Meurig ride together, Gwythyr leads & owns the telling, and Abisec's affinity-coordination is overshadowed. The affinity's discipline/communication (and Meurig's reliability as Abisec's man vs Gwythyr's pull) is a thing to tighten. Abisec banked the irritation, set it aside for the rebuild.

entries.name: GPC 483 — The Irish War (raids on Cornwall & western Logres; Gorlois defends)
entries.status: DECISIVE VICTORY (summer 483) — the ~800-raider summer offensive smashed in the surf at the long strand (Abisec's plan); coast secured for now
entries.dossier: GPC 483 spine: Irish sea-raiders harry Cornwall's coasts and WESTERN LOGRES; Duke Gorlois of Cornwall is fully occupied defending his duchy (the Irish are the real enemy — Gorlois is LOYAL, not the threat). Uther's court grows as he consolidates his nobles. RELEVANCE TO ABISEC: Hindon sits on the western march toward Summerland / the Severn approaches — the SAME western water the faceless MASTER's Bristol channel runs on. Irish raids on the western flank could touch his march or his affinity's coast, or tangle with the cross-water master-thread. Abisec (Battle 19, a banneret with an eschille + a sworn march affinity) is a natural muster for a western defence. Seeded w4 so the war LOOMS in oracle moments before its scheduled spring firing. — UPON THE MARCH (early winter 483): the seeded war broke EARLY under the Yule storm — 2 longships, ~80 raiders, burned a Summerland strand + a manor of Gwythyr's and are loose on the western water, wind-driven EAST toward Abisec's march. Gwythyr's coast ~2 days by land but they move by sea. Abisec — march protector, Battle 19, eschille + affinity — must choose: defend the threatened coast/affinity, or tend flood-stricken (and breached) Hindon first. — RESPONSE BEGUN (early winter 483): Abisec patched the breach, sent 2 knights (Sir Madog the cousin + Sir Gerin) west to BARON MEURIG to raise the affinity, and called his council. Word to go to UTHER (Hindon's Crown liege; the war is the King's matter) + Duke Gorlois (the King's western shield); Roderick informed as mentor/Stapleford-liege/neighbour. Council read [Alun]: 2 ships wind-driven east will hit the next soft strand — the BRUE MOUTH (Summerland's edge, the affinity's doorstep), ~a day's sail. [Senara — her father's march-lore]: the Brue shoals beach a ship only at HIGH TIDE — if the Brue, they come at the flood near dawn (the raiders' clock). — FIRST RAID BROKEN (early winter 483) [Q1 raiders-at-Brue ExcNo 99 · Q2 barons-muster ExcYes 13]: the raiders did NOT beach at the predicted Brue — cannier than a loot-raid, they slipped the watched tide and struck a chosen richer landing up the coast. GWYTHYR + MEURIG mustered ~40 lances and CRUSHED them (both ships burned, ~80 dead/taken) — a clean march victory, won WITHOUT Abisec (who held Hindon safe + raised Meurig's muster by his word, but struck no blow; Gwythyr crows that he held the march while the banneret sat behind his moat). UNEASE/HOOK [Senara]: 'they didn't move like raiders — someone told them where to go, and where NOT.' A guiding hand / inside knowledge — a thread toward the faceless master's western water, or a local betrayer. The GPC war continues through 483. — ESCALATION (early summer 483): the war returns bigger — a FLEET gathering off Ireland (10-20 hulls per rumor), the western/Summerland/Severn shore bracing for a season of fire. Gorlois holds Cornwall; the western march is Logres's soft underbelly. A war-council at Sarum; command of the western host contested (see 'the western command' thread). — DECISIVE VICTORY (summer 483): Abisec's surf-trap executed perfectly — recon confirmed the strand & dawn-flood [Battle 20 success], the held charge launched at the ideal instant [Fate Yes], and the host caught ~800 disordered Irish with their backs to the sea. Army Intensity collapsed in 2 rounds; the enemy routed INTO the water and drowned/died in the shallows. A crushing victory at a fraction of an open battle's cost. Gwythyr (leading the van Abisec ceded) keeps the public telling; the realm's commanders know whose plan won it. The western invasion broken; the war quiets (the GPC 483 Irish war recedes). Glory +90 → 3,140.

entries.name: GPC 483 — The Prince's Passion (court intrigue; Prince Madoc)
entries.status: RESOLVED (483 spring) — danger defused; Madoc a true patron; residue = Abisec is the prince's matchmaker
entries.dossier: GPC 483 keyed adventure (campaign/uther/06-adventures.md): a COURT-BASED INTRIGUE involving PRINCE MADOC (Uther's son, knighted 481) — a prince's passion/affair entangling the court. RELEVANCE: Abisec is a favoured banneret with restored royal trust; a court summons or a role around the prince's affair is plausible (a discreet errand, a witnessing, a faction pull). Seeded w3 as the year's court-thread; load specifics from the adventure when it activates. — IGNITED (483 spring, Sarum war-court): Madoc privately recruited Abisec to keep his affair with LADY INDEG of Drudwas QUIET (NOT marriage — appetite, not love [Fate No 66]). Betrothed = SIR GWILYM, a decent debt-bound old man (sympathetic, blind to her reluctance). Told the wronged man is GOOD, Madoc only HARDENED [Fate ExcNo 97] — a blind grateful husband = perfect cover; his patron-warmth chilled toward command. Abisec oath-bound to silence + protect the lady; cannot reach Indeg himself without scandal. Honest lever left: the lady's own agency, or Gwilym's hidden debt. — FLIPPED (Eluned's bower read, 483 spring): NOT a mutual love affair. Indeg is reconciled to / glad of the Gwilym match [Fate No 65] and does NOT love Madoc [Fate ExcNo 90] — she FEARS his pursuit, which she can't safely refuse and which threatens to ruin her, her marriage, her house, and Gwilym. No hidden bombshell [Fate No 87]. **Abisec's oath ('keep it quiet + protect the lady') now points OPPOSITE his patron: protecting Indeg = making Madoc STOP — the one thing the proud prince will never forgive. He was recruited under a false picture (mutual love) the prince told himself.** — RESOLVED (483 spring, Sarum): Abisec told Madoc the truth wrapped in grace — she's an honorable lady who wants the marriage, not an affair; you chose well; let me open other doors [opposed Courtesy 14+5=19 vs Proud 17 → WON, Madoc failed his resistance]. The prince accepted the face-saving exit, gave his WORD to leave Indeg alone, and came away a GENUINE patron (the canonical success: a powerful patron earned), warmer and owing Abisec for the dignity. Indeg safe; Gwilym's match & life-work safe; no scandal, no malcontent banner. Oath kept whole. Residue: Abisec promised to introduce Madoc to other eligible ladies (matchmaker obligation); Madoc now a real ally/patron. Glory +60 → crossed 3,000.

entries.name: Hindon storm-damage & the wall breach (rebuild)
entries.status: RESOLVED (held) — flood fully repaired by spring 483
entries.dossier: The Yule-storm flood of 483 gutted the lower wool-town: ~4 dead (Tegwen's family), 3 houses gone, the staple's lower wool-store ruined, ~12 new cattle drowned, and a BREACH torn in the new town wall (a DV gap, ~£10 to repair) — dangerously timed with Irish raiders on the water. Repairs ~£18 pending; the town's first deaths under Abisec's lordship (he fought the flood in the water with them — his standing held even in defeat). A live rebuild/defence burden. — EARLY WINTER 483: breach PATCHED for ~£1 [Mabli Stewardship CRIT] with the storm's own stone/timber + free town labor (DV ~3-4 there till the spring stone rebuild). Real bill ~£6 total (not £18); ~£5 waits for the thaw. Tegwen's people to bury. Abisec's standing held — he fought the flood in the water with his men. — (the raid passed Hindon by) the gathered folk can disperse home; the dead are buried; the ~£5 stone rebuild + mill + cattle wait for the spring thaw. — RESOLVED (spring 483): wall rebuilt in stone (DV5), mill mended, herd restocked off Cadwal (~£6 total); the dead mourned. Held at w0 (the loss remembered; the town's lord stood with them).

entries.name: The guided raiders — who steered the Irish? (hook)
entries.status: DORMANT but festering — Abisec chose NOT to hunt the local betrayer; the bow lies in the west, the coast leakable (will resurface)
entries.dossier: Early winter 483: the Irish raiders bypassed the Brue (where Senara's lore said they'd beach) and struck a chosen landing instead — moving 'like men who were told where to go, and where NOT' (Senara). Inside knowledge / a guiding hand on the western water. Candidates: the faceless MASTER (his Bristol cross-water channel — the same western water); a local betrayer; or canny raiders with a captured guide. Unproven — a thread to pull. The barons crushed the raiders before any of them could be questioned (the answer died on the strand, unless a roped survivor knows). — INVESTIGATED (483 spring; Meurig + march knights + Sir Gwion at Vagon) [Fate No 53 → NOT the faceless master's channel; Abisec Intrigue 11 → 7 success]: the raiders were AIMED at Cantlop strand (deep water at any tide — knowledge only ~3 march-men hold), so a LOCAL hand sold them the landing. Vagon's land-watch logged the lead: a stranger up-from-the-west-and-back in the raid-week, marked by a CHRONIC ILLNESS / OLD WOUND (shaking hands; a grey, wasting look) — no one caught his face, all caught his infirmity. **The betrayer is close to home — possibly within Abisec's own western-march affinity (a feasted man selling the coast to the Irish).** SEPARATE from the master-arc. NEXT: trace the marked man (west origin, who he serves). — LET GO (483 spring): Abisec deliberately declined the traitor-hunt — a coast always leaks, and tearing apart his own affinity over one marked man would cost more than it caught. He'll harden the watch by habit, not witch-hunt. CONSEQUENCE (PACING/no-softening): the local betrayer remains free, the coast leakable; the thread goes dormant but FESTERS — it will resurface (a future guided raid, the bow drawn again, the traitor emboldened). The marked-man lead (chronic illness/old wound, from the west) stays banked if ever reopened.

entries.name: The vanguard / place of honor (Irish war 483) — Gwythyr beat Abisec to it
entries.status: RESOLVED (held) — the strand victory won; Gwythyr led the van Abisec gave him, the commanders know the truth
entries.dossier: BORN (Turning Point, early summer 483, Sarum war-council). CORRECTED FEUDAL FRAME: the Irish war returns as a SUMMER OFFENSIVE — a fleet of 10-20 hulls = ~400-800 raiders (a small army, not a raid) on the western/Summerland/Severn coast. COUNT RODERICK holds OVERALL COMMAND of the combined regional host (a Count outranks every baron; the Rock of Sarum is the muster-base & strongest fortress; he commits the largest force). EACH LORD LEADS HIS OWN CONTINGENT under him (Gwythyr his, Meurig his, Abisec his eschille + sworn affinity). The CONTEST (the Turning Point) is the VANGUARD / PLACE OF HONOR / field-command of the decisive strike — who leads the killing-blow vs. who holds the line. GWYTHYR beat Abisec to it [Plot: Beat You To It], backed by the OLD GUARD (Caradoc: 'the van wants the surest hand on this coast — Gwythyr, twenty years & a victory; no shame to hold the line while the steady man strikes'). Galling, because the best field-soldier present by a clear head is ABISEC (Battle 20, the affinity, Bedegraine). Roderick presides — Abisec's backer, but must keep the prickly independent march barons sweet. STAKES: the glory of the strike, Abisec's standing, the march's safety. — WON (summer 483 council) [Abisec Battle 20 → CRITICAL vs Gwythyr's failed 16]: Abisec drew out Gwythyr's plan (sound for 2 ships, not 20), then dismantled it politely on its own logic and built a masterstroke — a fleet of ~800 can land in force at only 2 strands, only at the dawn flood, so CONCENTRATE the host and catch them IN THE SURF (half-ashore, unordered, backs to the sea). Undeniable; he won the VAN/field-command of the decisive strike on MERIT, not rank. The 'banneret behind his moat' slander is dead. — CEDED (summer 483): having won it, Abisec gave the van back to Gwythyr (your coast, your people) and took the right-hand role — a public grace that raised Abisec's standing again (old guard's glory-grabber fear killed) but did NOT disarm the shrewd Gwythyr [Fate No 72]. COMMAND in the battle: Gwythyr leads the van (B16) executing Abisec's plan, Abisec at his right hand (B20). RISK: the wary, un-disarmed rival holds the command — he may grab glory or half-heed counsel in the heat.

entries.name: The faceless hand — Elidyr's poisoner (strikes at Senara's blood)
entries.status: active MYSTERY — a professional, faceless killer; struck twice, escaped clean; Merlin knows the name & withholds it
entries.dossier: BORN summer 483 (Turning Point). A hidden hand tried twice to murder Sir Elidyr: a poisoned bolt (monkshood, thrice-drawn — a 'British art,' NOT foreign [Fate No] and NOT Gwythyr's pointed hand [Fate No]), then a night attempt at the Hindon sickbed that slew Gruffudd of the watch and escaped without a trace [ExcNo to capture]. MOTIVE (per Senara's read + Merlin's interest): the blow was aimed at SENARA — at her royal Ebbesborne blood — by removing Elidyr, i.e. to STOP the match. GOAL-ALIGNED with Merlin (who also opposes the match) though not proven the same hand. Merlin KNOWS the assassin's name and withholds it ('knowing it now would cost you more'). A skilled, patient, faceless enemy — and the next pull is the only cold lead: who profits if Senara's blood stays unwed to Throope. **RECOLOURED (scene 36):** Dwynwen's reading reframes the motive — the bolt struck at Senara's ISSUE, not the man: kill the sire (Elidyr) to stop the child the pact would 'wake.' Aligns the assassin's GOAL with Merlin's (control/prevent the issue) — same end, unproven same hand. Still faceless.

entries.name: The Ebbesborne changeling-pact (the summer house; midsummer; the door)
entries.status: active — the engine of the whole arc; midsummer clock running (6 days at scene 36)
entries.dossier: DISCOVERED summer 483 (the records failed → Senara's mother's song → Dwynwen's reading). The Ebbesborne royal blood is bound by a HOLLOW-HILL CHANGELING-BARGAIN — older than the Church — paid in children at MIDSUMMER at the line's old SUMMER HOUSE (a ruined villa a day into the Ebble hills). Held at bay by small prices: a SONG sung true (Senara's is half-lost — one line gone) and a food TABOO (never eat pork — Senara has kept it lifelong without knowing why). The old power's nature is ANTI-CIVILISATION ('the hollow ones want the thorn back in the wheat, the roof fallen in'); a fully-WOKEN scion of the blood 'opens the door.' THE STAKES = Senara's CHILD, not Senara — which is why MERLIN crosses a king to keep the issue under his hand, and (likely) why a FACELESS HAND twice tried to kill Elidyr (stop the sire). The line is FADING → the bargain comes DUE now. PROTECTION: the syncretic holy-house network (Iuan + abbeys owed favours: Ambrius/Brother Henris, Father Tewdric) = real aid. OPEN: how to shut the door FOR GOOD; the lost song-line; what waits at the house at midsummer; whether bringing Elidyr (the sire) there is folly. Party mustering in force (Abisec, Senara, Elidyr[frail], Custennin, Iuan, Dwynwen, Sir Jasson + lances, household). **AT THE SUMMER HOUSE (scenes 37-38):** abandoned, NO living keeper (Fate No) — the pact runs untended; the hollow is WRONG (hawthorn in untimely bloom, waiting for midsummer). Search ✓✓ (ruin: Spatial Flux + Military Outpost): THE DOOR = a sunken Roman water-shrine (a black spring); the house's space bends/thins toward midsummer. TWO old layers of keeping — the RITE (song+taboo = a small/gentle price, one child a lifetime apart) AND a GARRISON (the villa was fortified to HOLD the door by iron & men — repeatable; Abisec's read). Untended, on the long day the door opens WIDE & greedy (a child of the blood, or the hollow for the whole valley). THE FORK: (1) HOLD by force (garrison/bar/iron the shrine, hold the night — perilous, maybe only delay); (2) WORK THE RITE small — needs the LOST SONG-LINE + Senara as keeper; (3) SHUT FOR GOOD via the holy-house network (uncertain, maybe provoking). Senara's blood answers the place; her mother was the last keeper here (a personal thread). CLOCK: 5 days to midsummer. **PREP (scene 39, 5 days, ALL ✓):** FORCE — the villa refortified, door iron-barred & warded (Battle✓), holdable. RITE — the LOST SONG-LINE recovered (Dwynwen+Senara✓); the gentle rite is now performable, Senara as keeper. CHURCH — Ambrius sent a reliquary + a consecrating priest who's read of the door (✓); a permanent sealing can be attempted. PC-POSITIVE event: **Heledd** (the mother's old nurse) arrived & clarified the KEEPER'S PRICE = the keeper gives up her own childbearing (what the mother did). THE THREE ROADS at midsummer: (1) HOLD by force (buys this year only; lethal); (2) SING IT HOME — safe forever but Senara pays with her barrenness (no child of the blood → also voids Merlin's fear & the assassin's motive); (3) BREAK/SEAL via the Church relic (permanent & costless if it works, but may PROVOKE the power into ripping the door wide = the feared disaster). Force can underlie either. Heledd: Merlin watched the mother too (his interest predates Senara). MIDSUMMER = tomorrow. **DECISION (scene 40, council): SENARA CHOOSES THE RITE** — 'sing it home,' give up her childbearing — and reframes it past Elidyr's veto (not for him; for the valley & her own freedom). Plan: the rite at the turn of midsummer, force-fortified house + priest/relic as backup if she falls. Elidyr REFUSED to accept it (the lovers' rift now raw).
